source.name: MIL-HDBK-217F (Notice 2): base failure rates for electronic parts
source.title: Military Handbook: Reliability Prediction of Electronic Equipment
source.edition: Revision F (2 December 1991) with Notice 2 (28 February 1995)

licence.name: U.S. Government work (no copyright asserted)
licence.attribution: Source: MIL-HDBK-217F, Military Handbook: Reliability Prediction of Electronic Equipment (U.S. Department of Defense, 2 December 1991), with Notice 2 (28 February 1995). Distribution Statement A: approved for public release; distribution unlimited. A U.S. Government work; republished by Reliafy.
licence.note: A U.S. Department of Defense handbook. Both the handbook and Notice 2 carry Distribution Statement A ("Approved for public release; distribution unlimited") and no copyright notice; the official copies are free to download from ASSIST.

source.description: Base failure rates (λb) for electronic part types from the part stress models of the U.S. military's reliability prediction handbook, with each section's environment factors (πE) for its 14 use environments, from ground, benign to cannon, launch; and, from its parts count method (Appendix A), generic failure rates (λg) by environment with their quality factors (πQ) for microcircuits, laser diodes, motors, synchros and resolvers, circuit boards, quartz crystals and incandescent lamps.
caveats: A handbook prediction model, not failures counted in service: never mix it with field data.

Reliafy uses the base failure rate × the environment factor only (a parts-count record: the generic rate for the environment × the quality factor). The handbook's other factors (temperature, electrical stress, quality and more) aren't applied: each record names them, and real rates depend on them. Quality alone can move a rate by a factor of 10 or more.
The handbook covers electronic parts only: it has no batteries and no mechanical parts.
The models were last revised in 1995 and describe parts of that era; newer parts are often more reliable than the handbook predicts.
The handbook is guidance for comparing designs early, not a measure of how your equipment will fail.
source.table: The part stress models' base failure rate (λb) and environment factor (πE) tables, sections 5.6, 6, 8.1 and 9 to 23, and Appendix A's parts-count generic failure rates (λg) and quality factors (πQ) for microcircuits, laser diodes, rotating devices, circuit boards, quartz crystals and incandescent lamps

skipped.what: Microcircuits, part stress model (gate arrays, microprocessors, memories, VHSIC, GaAs)
skipped.reason: The model adds a die term and a package term (C1 πT + C2 πE), each from the device's complexity and package. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rates (Appendix A) by complexity band.

skipped.what: Microcircuits, VHSIC/VHSIC-like and VLSI CMOS
skipped.reason: Appendix A refers these to the section 5.3 model (die area, package, ESD rating): no generic rate.

skipped.what: Microcircuits, magnetic bubble memories
skipped.reason: The rate is a formula of the number of chips, loops and dissipative elements, and the duty cycle.

skipped.what: Microcircuits, hybrids
skipped.reason: The handbook gives no generic rate: each hybrid is unique, and its rate is the sum of the parts in it.

skipped.what: Diodes, low frequency: power rectifier with high voltage stacks
skipped.reason: The base rate is per junction (.0050 per junction): it needs the number of junctions.

skipped.what: Transistors, high frequency (low noise bipolar, high power bipolar, GaAs FET, Si FET)
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of frequency and output power (or a table of them), not one number per type.

skipped.what: Optoelectronics, alphanumeric displays
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of the number of characters and whether a logic chip is included.

skipped.what: Optoelectronics, laser diodes, part stress model
skipped.reason: The base rate depends on the material and on optical power and current. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rates (Appendix A).

skipped.what: Tubes (including travelling wave tubes and magnetrons)
skipped.reason: Not imported in this release: the base rates depend on tube type, power and frequency, and few designs use tubes now. Appendix A has no generic rates for tubes (it refers to section 7).

skipped.what: Lasers, carbon dioxide (sealed and flowing) and solid state (Nd:YAG, ruby)
skipped.reason: The rates are formulas of tube current, gas flow or the flashlamp's pulse energy and rate; Appendix A has no generic rates for lasers (it refers to section 8).

skipped.what: Rotating devices, motors, life model
skipped.reason: A life model for bearings and windings (characteristic lives by temperature), not a constant base rate. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rates (Appendix A, 10-year design life).

skipped.what: Rotating devices, synchros and resolvers, part stress model
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of the frame temperature. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rates (Appendix A).

skipped.what: Relays, mechanical
skipped.reason: The base rate depends on the ambient temperature (.0059 at 25 °C to .031 at 125 °C for a 125 °C rated relay): no one number per type.

skipped.what: Interconnection assemblies with plated through holes, part stress model
skipped.reason: The base rate is per plated through hole, weighted by the number of circuit planes: it needs the board's hole counts. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rate (Appendix A).

skipped.what: Interconnection assemblies, surface mount technology, part stress model
skipped.reason: A wear-out model in thermal cycles, not a constant base rate. Imported instead: the parts-count generic rate (Appendix A).

skipped.what: Quartz crystals, part stress model
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of frequency (.013 f^0.23). Imported instead: the parts-count generic rate (Appendix A, 50 MHz).

skipped.what: Lamps, incandescent, part stress model
skipped.reason: The base rate is a formula of rated voltage (.074 Vr^1.29). Imported instead: the parts-count generic rates (Appendix A).

skipped.what: Fiber optic cables
skipped.reason: The rate is per kilometre of fibre, a unit the library doesn't convert.

skipped.what: Microwave attenuators
skipped.reason: The handbook refers these to the resistor model (style RD).

skipped.what: Microwave fixed elements (directional couplers, fixed stubs and cavities)
skipped.reason: The handbook gives their rate as negligible, not a number.

skipped.what: Terminations (thin or thick film loads in stripline and thin film circuits)
skipped.reason: Given as 0.030 × πE without saying which environment table applies.

skipped.what: Parts count: discrete semiconductors, resistors, capacitors, inductive devices, elapsed time meters, relays, switches, connectors, connections, meters, filters and fuses
skipped.reason: Not imported in this release: the library has these parts' part stress base rates and environment factors instead.

skipped.what: Batteries and mechanical parts
skipped.reason: MIL-HDBK-217F covers electronic parts only: it has no batteries and no mechanical parts.

records.label: Lamp, incandescent, AC: generic failure rate (parts count)

failure_mode.name: Any failure
failure_mode.meaning: The part stops doing its job, in any way: the handbook's rate covers every failure mode together.

evidence.method: Handbook prediction model (generic failure rates by environment)

prediction.formula: λ = λg πQ (failures per million hours; λg for the environment)

not_applied.name: base rate (rated voltage)
not_applied.held_at: a 28 volt rating

not_applied.name: utilisation
not_applied.held_at: a utilisation rate of .5

citation.edition: Revision F (2 December 1991) with Notice 2 (28 February 1995)
citation.table: Appendix A, Generic Failure Rate λg for Inductive, Electromechanical and Miscellaneous Parts

licence.name: U.S. Government work (no copyright asserted)
licence.attribution: Source: MIL-HDBK-217F, Military Handbook: Reliability Prediction of Electronic Equipment (U.S. Department of Defense, 2 December 1991), with Notice 2 (28 February 1995). Distribution Statement A: approved for public release; distribution unlimited. A U.S. Government work; republished by Reliafy.

notes: Parts count (Appendix A): λ = λg × πQ, where λg is the handbook's generic failure rate for the environment (its part stress model at default values, environment included).
Appendix A's defaults: a utilisation rate of .5 and a 28 volt rating. The handbook gives no quality factor for lamps.
